name: Yodsira Accessibility Markup Audit
author: yodsira

sections.description:
Yodsira Accessibility Markup Audit does not add widgets to your site. It finds real markup problems — and, for safe categories, fixes the actual DOM after showing you exactly what will change.

The audit scans your homepage, latest posts and one static page (on a schedule or on demand) and reports:

  • images without alt text
  • skipped heading levels (h2 → h4) and multiple h1
  • links and buttons with no accessible name (icon-only links)
  • form fields without labels
  • pages that do not declare their language (<html lang>)
  • missing or empty <title>
  • generic link text (“read more”, “click here”)

Every issue comes with a severity and a one-phrase “how to fix” — the report is useful on its own, even if you fix everything by hand.

The repairs (each is a separate toggle):

Safe, on by default:

  • fill missing alt from the media library title/alt field
  • declare the page language on <html>
  • add scope to table headers

Risky, off by default — review the preview first:

  • accessible names for unlabeled controls (from URL slugs / placeholders)
  • titles for untitled iframes

Preview before anything goes live. The plugin records every attribute it would add — target, attribute, new value — and shows the list before you enable a repair. Nothing is ever removed from your markup; repairs only add attributes. When a repair has nothing to change, the page is served byte-for-byte unchanged.

Honest scope: automated checks catch a part of WCAG issues (roughly the mechanical 20–40%); contrast, focus order and ARIA patterns still need a human expert. Use it to keep the floor high and the report short.

Why not an overlay? Overlay widgets that inject toolbars and rewrite the page at runtime are rejected by the accessibility community: they don’t fix markup, sometimes break assistive tech, and create false confidence. Yodsira Accessibility Markup Audit is the opposite approach: find problems, fix the markup, show your work.

Pro Version

An optional companion plugin adds (one license = one site, 12 months of updates):

  • Client-ready compliance report — printable PDF with your findings and fixes
  • Weekly automatic rescans with a change digest
  • Agency white-label for reports

The free version is fully functional on its own and never limited.
Details: https://yodsira.com/product/a11yfix/

Yodsira Accessibility Markup Audit Pro

The companion plugin adds the client-facing layer on top of the free audit:

  • client-ready compliance report (print to PDF) with an agency white-label
  • weekly rescans of up to 25 pages with change digests
  • an honest “what automation does not cover” section

Buy Pro — $99/year

External Services

This plugin can send notifications ONLY to the service you configure in its
own settings. The only connection to the developer’s own service is the
optional, off-by-default error telemetry described below — nothing is sent
until you enable it yourself.

— Telegram notifications —
* What the service is: Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org), used to deliver
instant alerts to your own bot and chat.
* What data is sent and when: a short alert text with your site name and the
event details – sent only when the monitored event fires or when you press
the test button in settings.
* Opt-in: the feature is fully disabled until you enter your own bot token
and chat id; clearing them switches it off.
* Terms: https://telegram.org/tos
* Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy

  • Optional, off by default: anonymous error reports. If the admin enables
    the checkbox on the Audit page, a daily batch of sanitized scanner error
    signatures (message, file name:line, versions, site address) is sent to
    https://yodsira.com/api/telemetry so scan failures get fixed faster.
    Nothing is sent while the checkbox is off.
    Why: I am an independent developer, and this is the only way I learn about
    bugs I cannot reproduce myself. The free plugin makes no requests at all
    until you enable this option; when an error happens, an anonymous
    signature is sent to yodsira.com so I can fix it in the next release.
    Nothing else ever leaves your site, and you can switch it off at any
    moment. Every report is read by a human.
    Example of exactly what one report looks like (sanitized):

`message: “Call to a member function get_id() on null” — file: file.php:123 — culprit: plugin other-plugin — versions: plugin 0.2.3, WordPress 6.8, PHP 8.2
That is the whole payload — no content, no user data, no usage tracking.
Disabling telemetry clears any queued reports immediately.
Developer service terms: https://yodsira.com/en/terms/
Privacy policy: https://yodsira.com/en/privacy/

How the scan works

The daily scan fetches your site’s own pages over HTTP (the same way a
visitor’s browser would) and checks each page against nine concrete
rules, for example: images without meaningful alt text, links that
contain only an icon with no accessible name, buttons and toggles
missing state attributes, and headings that skip levels. The scan runs
from your own admin dashboard – no external service is involved and no
page content leaves the site. Findings are listed with the exact URL,
the rule that matched and a suggested fix you can preview before
applying.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the yodsira-accessibility-markup-audit folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open the Audit menu → press “Run scan now”.
  4. Review the report; enable repairs one by one, using Preview first.
sections.faq:
Will it slow my site down?

The scan runs on a cron request, never on a visitor’s page load. With only safe repairs on, enabled fixes run through native WordPress filters; the output-buffered DOM pass activates only when you enable DOM-level repairs, and pages without needed changes are returned untouched.

Can it break my layout?

Repairs only add attributes (alt, lang, scope, aria-label, title, value) and never touch tags, classes or styles. The preview shows every change before you enable a repair, and the front-end fixes have a master switch.

Is my site compliant after this?

No automated tool can promise compliance. The plugin fixes mechanical issues and produces a clear report; a full audit needs a specialist. Anything promising “one-click compliance” is selling you a lawsuit risk.

Where is my data stored?

Scan results live in your own database and the scanner crawls only your own site. The only outgoing connection is the optional, off-by-default error telemetry described in “External Services” — nothing is sent until you enable it.
